{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVdzeZs8AAAABbZd1GA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bpi2wzhE97X8", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bpi2w", "number": 5, "title": "MVP: Keyboard-controlled SOMA character driven by MotionBricks in Three.js/WebGPU", "body": "## Goal

Build a browser-based MVP that lets a user move a **freely usable SOMA humanoid character** with keyboard controls while **MotionBricks generates locomotion matching the user's movement intent**. Use **Three.js + WebGPU**, with inference running locally in the browser where supported.

## Scope

- Render a freely usable **SOMA-native skinned character** (prefer the native SOMA-X body asset; verify the precise model/asset license and redistribution terms before bundling it). Convert USD → glTF/GLB offline if necessary, keeping the skeleton and skinning intact.
- Load the pretrained **MotionBricks SOMA ONNX** model with ONNX Runtime Web's WebGPU execution provider; validate browser operator support and performance early. Do not treat TensorRT timings as WebGPU benchmarks.
- Support basic keyboard movement:
  - **WASD / arrow keys**: move (and turn or strafe, with documented controls).
  - **Shift**: run; no input: decelerate/stop/idle.
  - Optional orbit/follow camera for visibility.
- Translate user movement intent (desired velocity, heading, stop) into MotionBricks context/target poses, drawing on its official Scene Preview locomotion-target logic.
- Decode generated SOMA motion, apply root translation and joint rotations to the character, and continuously queue/blend generated segments during input changes.
- Show a simple ground plane, camera, and lightweight debug overlay (movement state, inference latency, generation/queue status).

## Implementation tasks

- [ ] Set up a minimal TypeScript + Three.js project with WebGPU-capable rendering.
- [ ] Choose a freely usable SOMA character; document asset provenance, license, and USD → GLB conversion steps (do not redistribute assets without permission).
- [ ] Verify the official SOMA ONNX model can load and run under ONNX Runtime Web/WebGPU; document any unsupported operators, memory constraints, or required conversions.
- [ ] Port the required MotionBricks SOMA pose encode/decode and target-generation logic from the official runtime.
- [ ] Map keyboard input to heading/speed (walk/run/stop) and generate motion segments from the resulting targets.
- [ ] Apply joint rotations/root motion to the skinned SOMA character and ensure smooth transitions across successive generations.
- [ ] Add camera, ground, control hints, and basic debug information.
- [ ] Document local setup, model acquisition, browser/GPU requirements, and known limitations.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The demo launches in a supported desktop browser and displays a skinned SOMA character (not only a stick-figure skeleton).
- [ ] Keyboard controls produce **MotionBricks-generated** walking/running/turning/stopping in the requested direction; this is not just a fixed pre-baked animation selected by keys.
- [ ] Motion remains continuous across successive generations and changes in movement input, without obvious resets/teleports.
- [ ] Inference executes locally using WebGPU; if incompatible, the blocking issue and reproduction details are documented explicitly rather than silently substituting prerecorded clips.
- [ ] README explains how to obtain the model assets legally and how to run the demo.

## Out of scope (initial MVP)

MMD/VRM retargeting, multiple characters, interactions with objects (jump/vault/sit), advanced physics, mobile optimization, and production-quality animation polish.

## References

- [MotionBricks](https://github.com/NVlabs/motionbricks)
- [MotionBricks Scene Preview](https://github.com/NVlabs/motionbricks/blob/main/docs/scene_preview.md)
- [MotionBricks ONNX inference](https://github.com/NVlabs/motionbricks/blob/main/docs/onnx_inference.md)
- [SOMA-X](https://github.com/NVlabs/SOMA-X)

**Licensing note:** SOMA-X code is Apache-2.0; check the actual character asset license separately.
